claims.claim: A dictionary is a mutable mapping from hashable keys to arbitrary objects.
A dictionary has one value per key; assigning an existing key replaces its associated value.
Direct subscription of an absent key raises KeyError, while get returns None or a supplied default.
Python dictionaries preserve insertion order, and updating a key does not move it.
Lists cannot be dictionary keys because they are mutable and not hashable.
Dictionary equality depends on having the same key-value pairs rather than their ordering.
